# Offline installs and mirrors

This page is for administrators and hosts whose servers have no outgoing internet access, or who want every
installation to use a tested copy of the packages. It explains how the installer behaves without the package server,
how to prepare an offline install, and how to run a mirror.

## Contents

1. [What the installer does without the server](#what-the-installer-does-without-the-server)
2. [Offline install, step by step](#offline-install-step-by-step)
3. [A local index.xml](#a-local-indexxml)
4. [Mirroring a release folder](#mirroring-a-release-folder)
5. [Pointing installations at the mirror](#pointing-installations-at-the-mirror)
6. [Keeping a mirror current](#keeping-a-mirror-current)
7. [Related pages](#related-pages)

## What the installer does without the server

The behavior comes from `kernel/setup/steps/ezstep_site_types.php`:

| Situation | Setup wizard | Kickstarter, `exp:install` |
|---|---|---|
| The index cannot be downloaded, `var/storage/packages/7x/index.xml` exists | that file is used instead, with no error | the same |
| The index cannot be downloaded, no local `index.xml` | "Retrieving remote site packages list failed. You may upload packages manually."; the imported site packages are still listed | the imported site package is used when all its required packages are imported; otherwise the step stops |
| A required package is not imported and cannot be downloaded | the step stops with an error naming the package | the same |
| Everything is imported | nothing is downloaded for the dependencies | nothing is downloaded |

So the reliable way to install offline is to **import every package first**. The kickstarter's documentation says
the same: "When the index cannot be read, a package already in the local repository is used if all its requirements
are imported (an offline install)" ([The kickstarter, 6.4](../../../install/06-kickstarter.md#64-kickstartini-reference)).

> **Note**
> A dry run (`exp:install --dry-run`, `exp:kickstarter run --dry-run`) always downloads the site package and its
> requirements into the temporary repository `var/storage/packages/dryrun/` to check them. It needs the package
> server (or a mirror) even when the packages are imported ([The kickstarter, 6.7](../../../install/06-kickstarter.md#67-dry-runs)).

## Offline install, step by step

On a machine with internet access:

1. Choose the site package, for example `sevenx_multisite_clean`.
2. Download it and every package it requires, and their requirements in turn
   ([Downloading a package by hand](downloading-a-package-by-hand.md#find-what-it-requires)). For
   `sevenx_multisite` these are `sevenx_classes` and `sevenx_multisite_democontent`.
3. Check each file ([Check it](downloading-a-package-by-hand.md#check-it)).

On the offline server, after the code is in place:

4. Copy the `.ezpkg` files to a folder of the installation, for example `var/tmp/packages/`.
5. Import each one:

   ```bash
   for f in var/tmp/packages/*.ezpkg; do php ezpm.php import "$f"; done
   ```

6. Check that they are in `var/storage/packages/7x/`:

   ```bash
   ls var/storage/packages/7x/
   ```

7. Install as usual: `exp:install --package=sevenx_multisite_clean`, the kickstarter with
   `[site_types] Site_package=sevenx_multisite_clean`, or the setup wizard, where the package appears as "Imported".
8. Remove the copies in `var/tmp/packages/` when the install is done.

## A local index.xml

When the index cannot be downloaded, the setup looks for `index.xml` in the system repository, the folder of
`[RepositorySettings] Vendor` (`var/storage/packages/7x/index.xml` by default), and uses it as if it had been
downloaded. That is useful when the `url` attributes in it point to a server the offline machine **can** reach, such as
a mirror in your own network. It does not make packages appear by itself: an entry whose `url` cannot be reached
still fails when it is needed.

> **Warning**
> In the setup wizard a site package entry from an index replaces the imported copy in the list when the index
> version is higher, and choosing it downloads the package again. A local index whose `url` cannot be reached can
> therefore hide your imported site package. Keep the versions in a local index equal to or lower than those of the
> imported packages, or use no local index.

## Mirroring a release folder

A mirror is a copy of one release folder on a web server you control. Nothing is needed but static file serving.

**From Git**, with only the folder you need:

```bash
git clone --filter=blob:none --sparse https://github.com/se7enxweb/exponential.packages.exponential.earth.git
cd exponential.packages.exponential.earth
git sparse-checkout set exponential/6.0/6.0.15
```

**From the server**, by its index:

```bash
base=https://exponential.packages.exponential.earth/exponential/6.0/6.0.15
mkdir -p mirror/6.0.15/thumbnails && cd mirror/6.0.15
curl -fsSLO "$base/index.xml"
grep -o ' url="[^"]*"' index.xml | cut -d'"' -f2 | xargs -n1 curl -fsSLO
grep -o 'thumbnail_url="[^"]*"' index.xml | cut -d'"' -f2 | (cd thumbnails && xargs -n1 curl -fsSLO)
```

Then rewrite the addresses in the copied `index.xml` to your host, because every `url` in the original names the
public server:

```bash
sed -i 's#https://exponential.packages.exponential.earth/exponential/6.0/6.0.15/#https://packages.example.com/6.0/6.0.15/#g' index.xml
```

Publish the folder so that `https://packages.example.com/6.0/6.0.15/index.xml` and every file it names answer `200`,
and check them ([Checking an index](the-index-xml-format.md#checking-an-index)). The 6.0.15 folder is about 87 MiB;
most of it is `sevenx_multisite_democontent.ezpkg`.

## Pointing installations at the mirror

```ini
# settings/override/package.ini.append.php
[RepositorySettings]
RemotePackagesIndexURL=https://packages.example.com/6.0/6.0.15
```

The setup wizard, the kickstarter, `exp:install` and ezupdate then use the mirror. ezupdate needs an `https://`
address. Details, including `kickstart.ini` and ezupdate's server list:
[Package server settings](package-server-settings.md) and
[Pointing a site at your package server](../your-own/pointing-a-site-at-your-package-server.md).

## Keeping a mirror current

Packages in a release folder are fixed in place on the public server: the file name stays, the content changes
([How a release reaches the package server](how-a-release-reaches-the-package-server.md)). To follow those fixes:

- with the Git mirror, `git pull` in the clone, then run the address rewrite again on `index.xml`;
- with the download mirror, run the download again into a new folder, compare checksums, and swap the folders.

Whether a mirror should follow every fix or stay at a version you have tested is your choice; a host that installs
many customer sites usually tests first.
